reason: H0 exclusively initializes and drives wuffs_json__decoder through fuzz_complex, fuzz_simple, and wuffs_aux::DecodeJson, so it cannot reach any std/nie decoder behavior. Although lack of NIE coverage existed in S0, S1 materially aggravates it by adding the new 'nïA' animated input format and a multi-frame decoder protocol with animation timing, skipping, counters, loop metadata, and restart state. Those newly introduced inputs and state transitions remain entirely unreachable under H0.
evidence: H0 defines WUFFS_CONFIG__MODULE__JSON and WUFFS_CONFIG__MODULE__AUX__JSON but no NIE module, and its decoding calls are wuffs_json__decoder__decode_tokens and wuffs_aux::DecodeJson.
S1 decoder.do_decode_image_config? newly recognizes 'nïA'le and sets this.animated = true, creating an animated-NIE input branch absent from S0.
S1 adds decoder.decode_animation_info?, which parses absolute durations and animation-loop terminators and validates embedded 'nïE' headers, nie_config, width, and height.
S1 adds decoder.skip_frame? and changes decoder.do_decode_frame_config? and decoder.do_decode_frame? to cycle through multiple frames using call_sequence states 0x20, 0x40, and 0x60.
S1 adds prev_duration, curr_duration, num_animation_loops_value, num_decoded_frame_configs_value, and num_decoded_frames_value, and changes restart_frame! to reset that state.
No function in H0 constructs wuffs_nie__decoder or invokes the base.image_decoder protocol methods changed in S1.
recommended_action: Add or extend a project-owned fuzz harness to instantiate the NIE decoder and drive decode_image_config, repeated decode_frame_config/decode_frame sequences, end-of-data handling, and restart_frame! across fuzz-controlled static and animated ('nïE'/'nïA') inputs, including chunked reads and animation timing/terminator fields.
